NOODLR.ChatPanel.Title: Noodlr - {name} (GM)
NOODLR.ChatPanel.InputPlaceholder: Talk to {name}… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
NOODLR.ChatPanel.NotConfigured: Chat provider not configured. Set the provider, model, and API key in module settings.
NOODLR.ChatPanel.HideOutputHint: When checked, the GM's reply stays in this panel: it is NOT mirrored to the players' chat log and is NOT spoken aloud on any other client. Applies to one prompt only — the box clears itself once the prompt is accepted — and the hidden reply is badged GM ONLY. Retrying a hidden reply keeps it hidden. Off by default. Your typed prompt is always private.
NOODLR.ChatPanel.RetryHiddenHint: Regenerate this reply. It stays GM-only: retrying a hidden turn never exposes it to the players, whatever the checkbox says now.
NOODLR.Chat.BudgetExceedsModel: Context token budget ({budget}) exceeds {model}'s context window ({limit} tokens). Lower the Context token budget in settings, or the model may truncate or reject long prompts.
NOODLR.Media.HideOutputHint: When checked, this result shows only on your screen (no broadcast, a GM-only card, and no shared playback). Use it to prep maps, handouts, or surprise NPCs. Off by default.
NOODLR.Artifact.RetryHint: Discard this output and generate a new one. Available for 60 seconds (GM, or the player who made it), then the output is committed to memory.
NOODLR.Artifact.RejectHint: Discard this output and commit nothing to memory. Available for 60 seconds (GM, or the player who made it).
NOODLR.Players.Title: Noodlr - {name}
NOODLR.Players.Intro: Ask about what your party already knows, or try your luck uncovering something hidden — you may be asked to make a roll.
NOODLR.Players.InputPlaceholder: Ask {name}… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
NOODLR.Players.P1Placeholder: Your question reached the GM's table. (Noodlr's player guide is being wired up — full answers arrive in the next update.)
NOODLR.Players.NoGM: No Gamemaster is online, so nobody can answer right now. Your question needs a connected GM - Noodlr answers players through the GM's client.
NOODLR.Players.GenFailed: The table guide couldn't answer just now — the GM's AI may be unconfigured or unreachable. Try again in a moment.
NOODLR.Players.Timeout: The table guide took too long to answer and gave up. The GM's AI provider may be slow or stalled — try again.
NOODLR.Players.NoAck: No Gamemaster's client picked this question up. A GM must be online with Noodlr enabled — Noodlr answers players through the GM's client. Ask your GM to check their console.
NOODLR.Players.NoReply: No answer came back. The GM's client may have disconnected or hit an error — ask your GM to check their console, then try again.
NOODLR.Players.RollPrompt: Give me a {skill} check from your character sheet, and we'll see what you turn up.
NOODLR.Provider.Provider.Name: Where the AI comes from (provider)
NOODLR.Provider.Provider.Hint: Pick OpenRouter (one account, one key, hundreds of models) or a Custom endpoint you run/host yourself.
NOODLR.Provider.BaseUrl.Name: Custom server address (base URL)
NOODLR.Provider.BaseUrl.Hint: Only needed for a Custom provider — the address of your OpenAI-compatible server, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.
NOODLR.Provider.ApiKey.Name: API key (password)
NOODLR.Provider.ApiKey.Hint: Your secret key for this provider. Required for OpenRouter; often optional for a local Custom server. Stored write-only: it is never shown again — leave blank to keep the saved one.
NOODLR.Provider.ApiKey.Saved: •••••••• saved — leave blank to keep it
NOODLR.Provider.CustomKey.Name: Custom endpoint key (password, optional)
NOODLR.Provider.CustomKey.Hint: Only for a Custom/local server that requires a key — most (Ollama, LM Studio, etc.) don't. OpenRouter features use the single shared key at the top of this window, not this field. Stored write-only.
NOODLR.Provider.OpenRouterKey.Name: OpenRouter API key (password)
NOODLR.Provider.OpenRouterKey.What: One key, entered once, used by every feature you set to the OpenRouter provider (chat, voice, images, music, video, embeddings, rerank).
NOODLR.Provider.OpenRouterKey.Requires: A free or funded account at openrouter.ai and its API key.
NOODLR.Provider.OpenRouterKey.Without: Any feature set to OpenRouter can't run. Features pointed at a local Custom server work without this.
NOODLR.Provider.Model.Name: Which model (slug)
NOODLR.Provider.Model.Hint: The exact model id, e.g. anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet. On OpenRouter, start typing to pick from the live list.
NOODLR.Provider.FetchNone: No list returned (check the URL/key, or type the value by hand).
NOODLR.Provider.FetchOk: {count} loaded — click the field to choose.
NOODLR.Feature.Chat.Title: Gamemaster Chat
NOODLR.Feature.Chat.What: The core AI Gamemaster you talk to — it narrates, answers, and rolls real Foundry dice.
NOODLR.Feature.Chat.Requires: A provider, a chat model, and (for OpenRouter) an API key.
NOODLR.Feature.Chat.Without: Nothing else in Noodlr works — this is the heart of the module.
NOODLR.Feature.Tts.Title: Spoken Voice (Text-to-Speech)
NOODLR.Feature.Tts.What: Reads the Gamemaster's replies out loud in a chosen voice.
NOODLR.Feature.Tts.Requires: A provider + a speech model + a voice name (and a key for OpenRouter).
NOODLR.Feature.Tts.Without: The GM still works perfectly, just silently — you read replies instead of hearing them.
NOODLR.Feature.Image.Title: Scene Art (Image Generation)
NOODLR.Feature.Image.What: Creates illustrations of scenes, places, and characters from a text description.
NOODLR.Feature.Image.Requires: A provider + an image model (and a key for OpenRouter).
NOODLR.Feature.Image.Without: No pictures are generated; everything else is unaffected.
NOODLR.Feature.Transcription.Title: Voice Transcription (Push-to-Log)
NOODLR.Feature.Transcription.What: Turns spoken table talk into text you can log and remember, when you press the record button.
NOODLR.Feature.Transcription.Requires: A provider + a speech-to-text model + a microphone (and a key for OpenRouter).
NOODLR.Feature.Transcription.Without: No automatic transcripts; you can still type everything yourself.
NOODLR.Feature.Music.Title: Music (Text-to-Audio)
NOODLR.Feature.Music.What: Generates thematic or combat music from a description and adds it to a Foundry playlist you can loop and fade.
NOODLR.Feature.Music.Requires: A provider + a music model (e.g. google/lyria-3-clip-preview) and a key for OpenRouter.
NOODLR.Feature.Music.Without: No AI music; you can still use your own playlists as normal.
NOODLR.Feature.Video.Title: Video (Text-to-Video, experimental)
NOODLR.Feature.Video.What: Generates a short clip (a few seconds) from a description and shows it to everyone — handy for a quick scare, trap, or comic beat.
NOODLR.Feature.Video.Requires: A provider + a video model (e.g. google/veo-3.1-fast) and a key for OpenRouter. Clips take longer and cost more than images.
NOODLR.Feature.Video.Without: No AI video; images and everything else are unaffected.
NOODLR.Feature.Rerank.Title: Rerank (Search Refinement)
NOODLR.Feature.Rerank.What: Re-scores the memory chunks found for a question and keeps only the most relevant, so the GM gets tighter context and spends fewer tokens.
NOODLR.Feature.Rerank.Requires: A provider + a rerank model (e.g. cohere/rerank-4-fast) and a key for OpenRouter. Only used when memory is on.
NOODLR.Feature.Rerank.Without: Memory still works using its own hybrid ranking; results are just a little less precise.
NOODLR.Feature.WebFallback.What: When the campaign's own memory has nothing confident to offer, let OpenRouter run a single web search for that one question and fold the results into the GM's answer.
NOODLR.Feature.WebFallback.Requires: The chat provider set to OpenRouter (it uses OpenRouter's web plugin, billed per search). Noodlr already disables OpenRouter's account-level Web Search on every chat request, so it only ever runs when this fallback fires - unless you enabled 'Prevent overrides' for the web plugin on OpenRouter, which blocks that.
NOODLR.Feature.WebFallback.Without: Off by default. Without it, the GM answers weak-memory questions from the model's own knowledge only — no live web lookups, no per-search cost.
NOODLR.Feature.Memory.What: Gives Noodlr a long-term memory so it recalls people, places, and events across sessions.
NOODLR.Feature.Memory.Requires: The separate noodlr-memory service running, reachable at its address, with a matching shared secret.
NOODLR.Feature.Memory.Without: Noodlr still plays, but forgets between sessions — it only knows the current conversation.
NOODLR.Feature.Embeddings.What: Converts text into the numeric form the memory needs to find related information.
NOODLR.Feature.Embeddings.Requires: Normally nothing here — the memory service handles it. Only fill this in to override it from Foundry.
NOODLR.Feature.Embeddings.Without: The memory service uses its own built-in embedding settings (recommended).
NOODLR.Settings.Enabled.Name: Enable Noodlr
NOODLR.Settings.Enabled.Hint: Turn Noodlr's features on or off for this world.
NOODLR.Settings.ChatContinueAfterRoll.Na: React to dice results (GM chat panel)
NOODLR.Settings.ChatContinueAfterRoll.Hi: Your assistant never rolls its own dice — it writes a macro and Foundry rolls it for real. But by then its reply is finished, so it has not seen the number. This sends the totals back once so it can narrate what actually happened. Turn it off and a reply that rolls dice ends at the bare result, with no outcome. Costs at most one extra request per turn, and Retry still resends your original message. Does not affect AI-run NPC turns.
NOODLR.Settings.AssistantName.Name: The GM assistant's name
NOODLR.Settings.AssistantName.Hint: What to call Noodlr's assistant in both chat panels and on the chat cards it posts. Up to 64 plain characters. Default: Polly Histor.
NOODLR.Settings.Ruleset.Name: Game rules system
NOODLR.Settings.Ruleset.Hint: Stated to every chatbot as fact, on every request. Without it a model deduces the system from adventure titles and place names — and published adventures are frequently converted between systems, so that guess is often wrong and always confident. Foundry can name the active system but not which revision you play (its id is the same for D&D 5e 2014 and 2024), so pick the exact one here.
NOODLR.Settings.Ruleset.CustomPlaceholde: Your system's name, up to 64 characters
NOODLR.Settings.Ruleset.SystemMismatch: {module} automates {system}, which is not the system this world is running. Noodlr will still use it if you pick it, but check that is what you meant.
NOODLR.Settings.Hooks.Detected: Rules automation is installed and will be listened to:
NOODLR.Settings.Hooks.None: No rules module is installed. Noodlr works as an AI game master and media generator, and the chatbots can still answer rules questions from your ingested books — but nothing enforces the rules, plays creatures, or reports what happened. Install a noodlr-hooks module for your game system to switch these on.
NOODLR.Settings.PromptsNote: Each box below arrives filled in with Noodlr's own wording, and whatever it contains is exactly what gets sent — nothing is added behind your back. Edit freely; Reset puts the shipped text back. Emptying a box sends no instructions at all for that role, which is rarely what you want.
NOODLR.Settings.ChatPromptHint: Governs the GM-only chat panel: how it narrates, adjudicates, tracks combat, and asks for rolls. Up to 65,000 characters.
NOODLR.Settings.PlayersPrompt.Name: Players' chat prompt
NOODLR.Settings.PlayersPrompt.Hint: Governs the players' chatbot: answers what the party already knows, and asks for a check before revealing anything hidden. This is the prompt that keeps it from handing out your secrets.
NOODLR.Settings.AdjudicationPrompt.Name: Roll adjudicator prompt
NOODLR.Settings.AdjudicationPrompt.Hint: Runs on your client after a player rolls: it compares their real total against GM-only memory and decides what they learn. Never seen by players.
NOODLR.Settings.ResetField.Label: Reset
NOODLR.Settings.ResetField.Hint: Put Noodlr's shipped text back in this field. Takes effect when you Save, so your other edits are safe.
NOODLR.Settings.TestNotConfigured: Chat provider is not configured yet.
NOODLR.Settings.TestEmpty: Provider responded, but with empty content.
NOODLR.TextGen.Menu.Name: Noodlr Text Generation
NOODLR.TextGen.Menu.Label: Text Generation
NOODLR.TextGen.Menu.Hint: The chat model, the assistant's name, every system prompt, and what gets injected into each request.
NOODLR.TextGen.Intro: Everything that shapes what Noodlr writes: which model answers, what it is told to be, and how much context it gets.
NOODLR.AudioGen.Menu.Name: Noodlr Audio Generation
NOODLR.AudioGen.Menu.Label: Audio Generation
NOODLR.AudioGen.Menu.Hint: Spoken narration (TTS), generated music, and voice transcription.
NOODLR.AudioGen.Intro: Sound in and out: narration read aloud to the table, generated music, and transcribing what everyone says at the table.
NOODLR.ImageGen.Menu.Name: Noodlr Image Generation
NOODLR.ImageGen.Menu.Label: Image Generation
NOODLR.ImageGen.Menu.Hint: Scene art, portraits, tokens, battlemaps, and video.
NOODLR.ImageGen.Intro: Four independent picture generators plus video. Each has its own model, style prompt, and size, because a token and a battlemap want nothing alike.
NOODLR.Security.Menu.Name: Noodlr Security
NOODLR.Security.Menu.Label: Security
NOODLR.Security.Intro: Credentials Noodlr stores for you. Keys are write-only: once saved, the stored value is never sent back to a browser — you can replace or clear it, not read it.
NOODLR.Security.NotesLegend: What your players can and can't see
NOODLR.Security.KeyExposureNote: Foundry replicates world-scoped settings to every connected client, so a determined player at your table could read this key from their own browser. Use a spending-capped OpenRouter key and rotate it if that matters to you — it is capped exposure, not a private secret.
NOODLR.Security.MediaUrlNote: Generated images, audio, and video are written into your Foundry data folder so they can be shared with the table. Anything saved there is reachable by anyone who can guess the URL, exactly like the rest of your world's assets.
NOODLR.Rag.Enabled.Name: Enable memory (RAG)
NOODLR.Rag.Enabled.Hint: Use the noodlr-memory service for long-term campaign memory. When off, Noodlr plays without recall.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.Name: How to reach the memory service
NOODLR.Rag.Target.Hint: A browser cannot open a Unix socket, so a service reached over a socket must be proxied by the web server that already serves Foundry. (noodlr-memory 1.1 and later also listen on a TCP port at the same time; earlier versions listened on the socket alone.)
NOODLR.Rag.Target.Proxy: Behind the Foundry server, at a path (recommended; required for Unix sockets)
NOODLR.Rag.Target.Direct: Direct URL to a TCP port
NOODLR.Rag.ServicePath.Name: Path on the Foundry server
NOODLR.Rag.ServicePath.Hint: The location your reverse proxy forwards to noodlr-memory, e.g. /memory. Requests go to Foundry's own address, so they inherit its TLS and are same-origin (no CORS). Nginx example: location /memory/ { proxy_pass http://unix:/run/noodlr-memory/noodlr-memory.sock:/; }
NOODLR.Rag.ServiceUrl.Name: Memory service URL
NOODLR.Rag.ServiceUrl.Hint: Full base URL of a TCP listener, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:3010. NOODLR_MEMORY_HOST must be bound to an address your browser can reach (127.0.0.1 only serves the service's own machine) and NOODLR_MEMORY_PORT must not be 0.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.NoPath: No path set. Enter the location your web server forwards to noodlr-memory, e.g. /memory.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.NoUrl: No URL set. Enter the address of the memory service, or switch to the proxy option above.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.BadUrl: That doesn't parse as a URL. It should look like http://host:3010.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.Loopback: 127.0.0.1 means the computer running this browser, not the Foundry server at {host} — so this only works when Foundry and noodlr-memory are on the machine you're sitting at. Use the proxy option above, or the Foundry host's real address.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.MixedContent: Foundry is served over HTTPS but this URL is HTTP, and browsers block that mix except for localhost. Use the proxy option above, or put the service behind HTTPS.
NOODLR.Rag.Target.ProxyFailed: Foundry's own address answered, but not at this path. Check that your web server has a location block for it and that noodlr-memory is running (systemctl status noodlr-memory).
NOODLR.Rag.Target.DirectFailed: Nothing answered there. Usual causes: the service is bound to 127.0.0.1 on a different machine (set NOODLR_MEMORY_HOST to a reachable address), it has no TCP listener at all (NOODLR_MEMORY_PORT=0, or a noodlr-memory older than 1.1 with NOODLR_MEMORY_SOCKET set), or a firewall is in the way.
NOODLR.Rag.Secret.Name: Memory shared secret
NOODLR.Rag.Secret.Hint: Value of x-noodlr-secret; must match the service's NOODLR_MEMORY_SECRET.
NOODLR.Rag.Hybrid.Name: Hybrid retrieval
NOODLR.Rag.Hybrid.Hint: Dense + BM25 fusion with importance/recency re-rank. Off = pure semantic.
NOODLR.Rag.AgentMode.Name: Agent Mode retrieval
NOODLR.Rag.AgentMode.Hint: Use the chat model to decompose each query into multiple sub-queries + entities before searching.
NOODLR.Rag.SendEmbedConfig.Name: Send embedding config from Foundry
NOODLR.Rag.SendEmbedConfig.Hint: Send the module's embedding provider/model/key per request. Off = the service uses its own .env (recommended, keeps keys server-side).
NOODLR.Rag.TokenBudget.Name: Retrieval token budget
NOODLR.Rag.TokenBudget.Hint: Approximate max tokens of retrieved memory injected into each prompt. 4000 suits large-context models; typical RAG setups allocate anywhere from 2500 to 25000 to knowledge. Raise it for richer recall, but it must fit inside the overall Context token budget alongside the system prompt and chat history.
NOODLR.Rag.TopK.Name: Results per query (topK)
NOODLR.Rag.TopK.Hint: How many passages to retrieve before budgeting. This is the ceiling on how many chunks CAN be injected - set it high enough to actually fill the token budget (e.g. ~8-12 chunks to fill 4000 tokens). Extra chunks beyond the budget are dropped.
NOODLR.Rag.WebFallback.Enable.Name: Fall back to a web search when memory is unsure
NOODLR.Rag.WebFallback.Enable.Hint: Only fires on OpenRouter chat, and only for the one request where memory came up short. Each search adds a small OpenRouter charge. Leave off if your world is purely fictional (the web rarely helps).
NOODLR.Rag.WebFallback.MinScore.Name: Confidence threshold (0-1)
NOODLR.Rag.WebFallback.MinScore.Hint: 0 = only search when memory returns nothing. Raise it to also search when the best match is weak. Scores are backend-scaled, so tune by watching results.
NOODLR.Rag.WebFallback.MaxResults.Name: Max web results
NOODLR.Rag.WebFallback.MaxResults.Hint: How many search results to fold in (1-10). More results = more grounding but more tokens/cost.
NOODLR.Rag.ChatLog.Enable.Name: Record the Foundry chat log to memory
NOODLR.Rag.ChatLog.Enable.Hint: Distills every native chat message (talk, rolls, skill checks, spells, loot, etc.) into timestamped text and ingests it into the 'unfiltered_chat' silo — turning Foundry's own log into searchable long-term campaign memory. Only the GM's client records; Noodlr's own cards are skipped. Off by default.
NOODLR.Rag.ChatLog.Whispers.Name: Include whispers
NOODLR.Rag.ChatLog.Whispers.Hint: Whispers are private (even a GM can't see whispers they aren't part of). Off by default; turn on only if you want private messages recorded into memory too.
NOODLR.Rag.ChatLog.Interval.Name: Flush interval (seconds)
NOODLR.Rag.ChatLog.Interval.Hint: How often buffered chat lines are written to memory as one batch (30–3600; also flushes early during busy combat). Batching keeps embedding calls efficient.
NOODLR.Rag.Menu.Name: Noodlr Memory Configuration
NOODLR.Rag.Menu.Label: Memory Configuration
NOODLR.Rag.Menu.Hint: Long-term memory: connection, retrieval, embeddings, and transcripts.
NOODLR.Rag.Manage.Label: Manage Memory (silos & ingest)
NOODLR.Rag.ConfigIntro: Everything about Noodlr's long-term memory lives here. Pick a memory backend, choose how it recalls information, and open the Manage Memory and Diagnostics tools. (Lorebook and the Memory browser live on the Noodlr toolbar.)
NOODLR.Rag.Backend.Name: Memory backend
NOODLR.Rag.Backend.Hint: Where memories are stored and searched. RAG Lite runs entirely inside Foundry (nothing to install); noodlr-memory is a separate service you host for shared, higher-capacity memory. Options that don't apply to the chosen backend are grayed out below.
NOODLR.Rag.Backend.LiteNote: RAG Lite is active: memory lives in this world's data folder and is embedded in your browser with a bundled model — no service URL, secret, or API key needed. It runs on the GM's client only. Use the Diagnostics window's "Test in-browser embedder" to confirm it loads.
NOODLR.Rag.Backend.LiteEmbedNote: RAG Lite embeds text in your browser with the bundled all-MiniLM model (384-dim), so the embedding provider/model settings below don't apply. Switch to the noodlr-memory backend to configure a custom embedding model.
NOODLR.Rag.Offline: Noodlr memory service is unreachable — continuing without long-term memory.
NOODLR.Rag.NotEnabled: Memory (RAG) is not enabled. Enable it and set the service URL in settings.
NOODLR.Rag.ResetConfirm: Permanently delete all memories in the "{silo}" silo? This cannot be undone.
NOODLR.Rag.IngestHint: Pick a target silo per compendium and ingest its documents (locked or unlocked).
NOODLR.Rag.NoPacks: No compendium packs found in this world.
NOODLR.Rag.Upload: Upload TXT / JSON / YAML / CSV / PDF
NOODLR.Rag.UploadHint: Upload a file to ingest into a silo. TXT/Markdown ingest as-is. JSON, YAML, and CSV are split into one memory per record (array item, object, or row) so searches return the individual entry. PDF works only on the noodlr-memory backend (RAG Lite can't read PDFs — convert to .txt).
NOODLR.Rag.StructuredEmpty: No records found in that file — check it's valid JSON/YAML/CSV with at least one entry (CSV needs a header row).
NOODLR.Rag.Queue.Hint: Ingests run one at a time, in the order you start them. Click as many compendiums as you like — two at once would only halve each one's share of your embedding provider's rate limit. A run keeps going if you close this window, and an unfinished compendium picks up where it stopped after a page reload.
NOODLR.Rag.Queue.Resumed: Resuming {count} unfinished ingestion job(s) from before the reload.
NOODLR.Rag.Queue.NoResume: Nothing to resume — no documents were stored, so start it again instead.
NOODLR.Rag.Queue.RateLimited: provider rate limit — waiting {seconds}s before retry {attempt}
NOODLR.Rag.EmbedBatchSizeHint: How many texts go in each embedding request (0 = let the service decide). A rate limit counts REQUESTS, not texts, so this is the first thing to raise when a provider says 429: 16 → 64 is the same work in a quarter of the calls. Too high and the provider may reject the payload instead; the service splits oversized batches by length, so start at 64.
NOODLR.Rag.EmbedPaceMsHint: Deliberately slow every embedding request down by at least this long (0 = no floor). Only needed for a provider with a strict per-minute limit: the service already paces itself after it sees a 429, so leave this at 0 unless ingestion still stalls.
NOODLR.Dev.ExportHint: Download the ticked compendiums as JSONL, keeping the full rules text and the complete system data side by side. Creatures are expanded: every trait, action, reaction and legendary action becomes its own line, since that is where a rule actually lives. This is not ingestion — nothing is embedded, nothing is sent anywhere, and memory is untouched. The files are input for the offline rules miner. Adventure books are worth including for their unique creatures, though they yield far less than the rulebooks.
NOODLR.Dev.ExportNoPacks: Tick at least one compendium to export.
NOODLR.Dev.ExportWhere: Each compendium becomes a download link below as it finishes. Click every link to save the files — browsers refuse to save a batch of files on their own, so this is the only way to get all of them. Links stay valid until you close this window.
NOODLR.Dev.ExportDone: Built {packs} compendium(s): {documents} documents → {records} records, {size} MB. Click each link below to save it.
NOODLR.Prompt.AuthorNote.Name: Author's note (session anchor)
NOODLR.Prompt.AuthorNote.Hint: Injected near the end of the conversation at the configured depth: current location, time, party status, active threats, tone.
NOODLR.Prompt.PostHistory.Name: Post-history instructions
NOODLR.Prompt.PostHistory.Hint: A short instruction block placed as the very last message every turn.
NOODLR.Prompt.CombatReminder.Name: Combat reminder
NOODLR.Prompt.CombatReminder.Hint: Swapped into the post-history slot automatically while Foundry combat is active.
NOODLR.Prompt.AuthorNoteDepth.Name: Author's note depth
NOODLR.Prompt.AuthorNoteDepth.Hint: How many messages from the end to inject the author's note before (default 3).
NOODLR.Prompt.ContextBudget.Name: Context token budget
NOODLR.Prompt.ContextBudget.Hint: Approximate max tokens for the WHOLE assembled prompt (system prompt + lorebook + retrieved memory + Foundry state + chat history); older history is trimmed to fit. 12000 is deliberately thrifty. With large-context models (200k-1M) you can safely raise this to 32000-64000+ to keep more of the recent conversation in play - but cost and latency scale with every token you send each turn, and RAG + Lorebook already backstop long-term recall, so there's rarely a reason to go near the model's true maximum. Watch Diagnostics 'Avg/Peak context sent' to tune it.
NOODLR.Prompt.ChatMemoryWrites.Name: Memory writes
NOODLR.Prompt.ChatMemoryWrites.Hint: Let the assistant record, revise, or remove long-term memory facts on its own when it establishes durable world-state. Every write is confined to the allowed silos and whispered to the GM as an audit line. Requires memory (RAG) enabled. Disable to keep all memory edits manual (via the Memory browser).
NOODLR.Prompt.DebugLogging.Name: Verbose debug logging (this browser)
NOODLR.Prompt.DebugLogging.Hint: Log detailed diagnostics to this browser's developer console (F12): the full prompt sent to each chatbot, whether the Tipster scene briefing and memory context were injected, the player question relay, and raw replies. Affects only your own browser. Leave off for normal play - prompts can be long.
NOODLR.Prompt.DeveloperMode.Name: Developer tools (this browser)
NOODLR.Prompt.DeveloperMode.Hint: Show tools meant for building Noodlr itself, not for running a game. Currently this adds a compendium export to the Manage Memory window, which writes complete rulebook documents to disk for offline analysis. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing changes about play. Affects only your own browser; leave off unless you were asked to turn it on.
NOODLR.Prompt.TipsterGm.Name: Scene awareness (GM chat)
NOODLR.Prompt.TipsterGm.Hint: Quietly tell the assistant what's happening in the active scene right now — scene name and size, in-world date/time, lighting and darkness, ambient sound and the playing track, named regions, and the token roster. Read fresh from Foundry on every message and never stored, so it can't go stale. Costs roughly 100-250 tokens per message.
NOODLR.Prompt.TipsterPlayers.Name: Scene awareness (players' chat)
NOODLR.Prompt.TipsterPlayers.Hint: Same live scene briefing for the players' chatbot, built from the perspective of whichever player is asking. Only non-secret surroundings are included — no hidden tokens, no secret doors, no GM notes.
NOODLR.Lorebook.Menu.Name: Noodlr Lorebook
NOODLR.Lorebook.Menu.Label: Edit Lorebook
NOODLR.Lorebook.Menu.Hint: Manage keyword/constant World Info entries injected into the prompt.
NOODLR.Lorebook.Title: Lorebook / World Info
NOODLR.Lorebook.Intro: Entries activate by keyword (plaintext or /regex/) or are always-on (constant). Activated entries are injected as World Info.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.Title: Memory browser (RAG)
NOODLR.RagBrowser.Intro: Search any memory collection, then edit or delete individual records, or add new ones by hand. Player-visible collections can be read by the players' bot; GM-secret collections never are.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.Empty: No matching records. Try a different search or collection.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.Prompt: Enter a search term and pick a collection, then Search.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.Disabled: Memory (RAG) is not enabled. Turn it on in Memory & Knowledge first.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.DeleteConfirm: Permanently delete this record from the collection?
NOODLR.RagBrowser.RetractHint: Mark this record as a known error. It stays here for reference but is never given to a chatbot again.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.RetractConfirm: Mark this record as a known error? It stays in the collection so you can see what went wrong, but retrieval will skip it from now on. Use Delete instead if you want it gone entirely.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.Retracted: Record retracted in "{silo}" — it will no longer be retrieved.
NOODLR.RagBrowser.RetractedHint: Marked as a known error. Kept for reference; never retrieved.
NOODLR.Media.TtsEnabled.Name: Enable TTS
NOODLR.Media.TtsEnabled.Hint: Allow Noodlr to synthesize speech via the TTS provider.
NOODLR.Media.TtsVoice.Name: TTS voice
NOODLR.Media.TtsVoice.Hint: Default voice id/name for speech (see your provider's voice list).
NOODLR.Media.TtsAutoRead.Name: Read GM replies aloud
NOODLR.Media.TtsAutoRead.Hint: Automatically speak each GM chat reply on this client.
NOODLR.Media.TtsBroadcast.Name: Play speech for everyone at the table
NOODLR.Media.TtsBroadcast.Hint: Play generated speech on every connected player's browser, not just the one that made it. Leave this on for remote tables. Turn it off for in-person play, where several browsers in one room will echo.
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.Name: Test voice output
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.Hint: Edit this phrase if you like (up to 140 characters), then Test to synthesize and play it using your SAVED TTS settings (save first if you just changed them). Emptying the box puts the default phrase back, since there is nothing to speak otherwise. The result or error appears below — handy because audio problems are often unrelated to the provider.
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.Placeholder: Type a short phrase to hear it spoken…
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.Sample: Hearing spoken audio confirms a successful test of text-to-speech capability.
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.NotConfigured: TTS isn't configured yet. Set a provider, model, and (for OpenRouter) an API key, then Save before testing.
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.Ok: Success — received {kb} KB ({type}). Playing now. If you hear nothing, it's a local audio/output issue on this machine, not the TTS provider.
NOODLR.Media.TtsTest.Network: Could not reach {endpoint} from your browser. Usual causes: mixed content (Foundry is HTTPS but the TTS URL is HTTP — browsers allow that only for localhost/127.0.0.1), missing CORS headers on the TTS server (it must return Access-Control-Allow-Origin), or the URL simply isn't reachable from this machine. Putting the TTS endpoint behind your HTTPS reverse proxy fixes all three.
NOODLR.Media.ImageExpand.Name: Expand image prompts
NOODLR.Media.ImageExpand.Hint: Send your short description to the chat model first and let it write the fuller art prompt, using the instructions below. Costs one extra chat call per picture.
NOODLR.Media.ImageSystemPrompt.Name: Prompt-expansion instructions
NOODLR.Media.ImageSystemPrompt.Hint: How the chat model should rewrite your description into an art prompt. Only used when "Expand image prompts" is on; if you empty this field, your description is sent to the image model untouched.
NOODLR.Media.ImageSteps.Name: Sampling steps
NOODLR.Media.ImageCfg.Name: CFG scale
NOODLR.Media.ImageSampler.Name: Sampling method
NOODLR.Media.ImageSampler.Hint: Sampler name, e.g. Euler a (SD-compatible endpoints).
NOODLR.Media.ImageSeed.Name: Seed
NOODLR.Media.ImagePositive.Name: Positive style prompt (prepended)
NOODLR.Media.ImagePositive.Hint: A style phrase added in front of every image, e.g. "dark fantasy oil painting, dramatic lighting". This keeps all your art looking consistent; the scene's subject is added after it.
NOODLR.Media.ImageNegative.Name: Negative prompt (things to avoid)
NOODLR.Media.ImageNegative.Hint: What you never want in the picture, e.g. "text, watermark, blurry, extra limbs". Used by Stable-Diffusion-style servers.
NOODLR.Media.ImageSize.Name: Image size
NOODLR.Media.ImageSize.Hint: Pick a standard pixel size for this generator. Smaller sizes are faster and cheaper; larger ones show more detail. If a model rejects a size or gives odd results, choose 'Default (model's native size)' to let it decide, or 'Custom' to type your own width x height. Images are saved as .webp at whatever resolution the model returns.
NOODLR.Media.MapUpscale.Name: Upscale to 4x (coming soon)
NOODLR.Media.MapUpscale.Hint: Will slice the generated map and run each piece through an image upscaler to produce a much larger, high-detail battle map, then stitch it back together seamlessly. Disabled for now: it needs a dedicated super-resolution model, which OpenRouter does not yet offer. Planned for when that capability becomes available.
NOODLR.Media.ImageSubfolderNote: Saved under your media folder in:
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Image.Title: Scene Art (Generate Image)
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Image.What: Illustrates scenes, places, and moments from a description. Chat: "Generate Image: a rain-soaked harbor at dusk".
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Image.Requires: The shared OpenRouter key (or a Custom image endpoint) + an image model.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Image.Without: No scene art is generated; everything else is unaffected.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Portrait.Title: Portrait (Generate Portrait)
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Portrait.What: A waist-up character portrait, saved as a 1000×1000 .webp for continuity. Chat: "Generate Portrait: a lithe half-elf rogue with silver hair".
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Portrait.Requires: The shared OpenRouter key (or a Custom image endpoint) + an image model.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Portrait.Without: No portraits are generated; use Scene Art or your own art instead.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Token.Title: Token (Generate Token)
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Token.What: A top-down / isometric actor token, saved as a 400×400 .webp. Chat: "Generate Token: a snarling dire wolf".
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Token.Requires: The shared OpenRouter key (or a Custom image endpoint) + an image model.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Token.Without: No tokens are generated; drop in your own token art instead.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Token.Prompt: Describe the actor for a top-down token.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Map.Title: Map (Generate Map)
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Map.What: A top-down / isometric walkable scene map, saved as a .webp. Chat: "Generate Map: a ruined keep courtyard". Default 4500×6000; editable (450–7800 per side).
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Map.Requires: The shared OpenRouter key (or a Custom image endpoint) + an image model.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Map.Without: No maps are generated; build scenes with your own map art.
NOODLR.Media.Kind.Map.Prompt: Describe the walkable map to generate.
NOODLR.Media.ImageParamsNote: The steps / CFG / sampler / seed values only matter for Stable-Diffusion-style servers; OpenRouter and OpenAI-style image models ignore them.
NOODLR.Media.ImageFolder.Name: Where to save generated images
NOODLR.Media.ImageFolder.Hint: A folder under Foundry's data area. Default assets/noodlr-out is created automatically. Browse to pick or make another — you can't go above the data folder, and Foundry blocks saving into modules/systems/worlds.
NOODLR.Media.ImageFolder.NoPicker: Foundry's file picker isn't available; type the folder path by hand.
NOODLR.Media.ImagePersist.Name: Save images to disk (keep for continuity)
NOODLR.Media.ImagePersist.Hint: What it does: writes each generated image to the folder above and remembers a recurring character/location's look (seed + description) so it stays recognizable. What it needs: write access to the data folder (GM). Without it: images still display, but nothing is kept and portraits may drift between scenes.
NOODLR.Media.ImageChatTrigger.Name: Enable chat commands for images
NOODLR.Media.ImageChatTrigger.Hint: Type in chat: "Generate Image: a rain-soaked harbor at dusk" for a one-off, or "Generate Portrait: Vex: a lithe half-elf rogue with silver hair" to make a reusable, consistent portrait. The image pops up for everyone at the table.
NOODLR.Media.ImageAllowPlayers.Name: Let players trigger images too
NOODLR.Media.ImageAllowPlayers.Hint: What it does: allows non-GM players to use the chat commands above. What to know: each image costs API money, so this is off by default. Without it: only the GM can generate images.
NOODLR.Media.Image.GMOnly: Only the GM can generate images (enable player triggers in Noodlr settings to change this).
NOODLR.Media.TtsPitch.Name: My TTS endpoint accepts a pitch parameter
NOODLR.Media.TtsPitch.Hint: Leave OFF for OpenRouter and most OpenAI-style servers (they'd reject an unknown 'pitch' field). Turn ON only for a custom endpoint you know accepts pitch — then per-creature pitch below is sent through.
NOODLR.Media.CreatureVoices.Name: Per-creature voices
NOODLR.Media.CreatureVoices.Title: Creature-type voices
NOODLR.Media.CreatureVoices.Hint: Assign a voice (and optional pitch %) to each creature type. When Noodlr speaks for an NPC/monster, it uses the voice for that creature's type (falling back to the base type, then the default voice). Pitch is only sent if 'My TTS endpoint accepts a pitch parameter' is ticked.
NOODLR.Media.TranscriptionEnabled.Name: Enable voice transcription (push-to-log)
NOODLR.Media.TranscriptionEnabled.Hint: What it does: shows the floating microphone button so participants can click-to-record; speech is transcribed to text, optionally posted to chat, logged to the session journal, and ingested into memory. What it needs: a transcription model/endpoint + mic permission. Without it: no mic button and no transcription.
NOODLR.Media.MusicPromptHint: Describe the mood/scene (e.g. "tense dungeon ambience with low drums").
NOODLR.Media.VideoPromptHint: Describe the short clip (e.g. "a torch sputtering out in a dark crypt").
NOODLR.Media.MusicEnabled.Name: Enable music generation
NOODLR.Media.MusicEnabled.Hint: What it does: lets the GM generate mood/combat music. What it needs: a music model + key. Without it: no AI music.
NOODLR.Media.MusicPlaylist.Name: Playlist name
NOODLR.Media.MusicPlaylist.Hint: Generated tracks are added to (and this playlist is created if missing) so you can loop, fade, and reuse them.
NOODLR.Media.MusicMin.Name: Min seconds
NOODLR.Media.MusicMax.Name: Max seconds
NOODLR.Media.MusicDurationNote: Length is a hint passed to the model — some music models produce a fixed-length clip (often ~30s) regardless.
NOODLR.Media.MusicTrigger.Name: Enable 'Generate Music:' chat command
NOODLR.Media.MusicTrigger.Hint: Type in chat: "Generate Music: tense dungeon ambience with low drums".
NOODLR.Media.MediaAllowPlayers.Name: Let players trigger this too
NOODLR.Media.MediaAllowPlayers.Hint: Off by default — generation costs API money, so normally only the GM can trigger it.
NOODLR.Media.Music.NoSave: Music was generated but couldn't be saved to disk (need GM upload permission).
NOODLR.Media.Music.NoPlaylist: Couldn't add the track to a playlist; it was still saved to disk.
NOODLR.Media.VideoEnabled.Name: Enable video generation (experimental)
NOODLR.Media.VideoEnabled.Hint: What it does: lets the GM generate a short clip shown to everyone. What it needs: a video model + key. Without it: no AI video. Note: slow and comparatively expensive.
NOODLR.Media.VideoDuration.Name: Duration (sec)
NOODLR.Media.VideoResolution.Name: Resolution
NOODLR.Media.VideoAspect.Name: Aspect ratio
NOODLR.Media.VideoDurationNote: Most models support ~4–15s; 6–30s is requested and clamped, but the provider may cap it lower.
NOODLR.Media.VideoTrigger.Name: Enable 'Generate Video:' chat command
NOODLR.Media.VideoTrigger.Hint: Type in chat: "Generate Video: a torch guttering as something moves in the dark".
NOODLR.Media.Video.Generating: Noodlr: generating video (this can take a while)…
NOODLR.Media.Video.NoSave: Video was generated but couldn't be saved to disk (GM upload permission required); not shared.
NOODLR.Rag.Rerank.Enable.Name: Refine results with a rerank model
NOODLR.Rag.Rerank.Enable.Hint: After memory returns matches, a rerank model re-scores them for relevance and keeps the best few. Improves precision and can save chat tokens.
NOODLR.Rag.Rerank.TopN.Name: Keep top N after rerank
NOODLR.Rag.Rerank.TopN.Hint: How many of the reranked chunks to inject into the prompt.
NOODLR.Media.PushIngestElsewhere: Whether transcripts are saved into long-term memory is set in the Memory & Knowledge window.
NOODLR.Media.PushPostChat.Name: Post transcripts to chat
NOODLR.Media.PushPostChat.Hint: Post each transcribed segment to the Foundry chat log.
NOODLR.Media.PushIngest.Name: Ingest transcripts to memory
NOODLR.Media.PushIngest.Hint: Periodically ingest the session transcript into the chat silo.
NOODLR.Media.PushIngestInterval.Name: Ingest interval (seconds)
NOODLR.Media.PushIngestInterval.Hint: How often to flush the transcript buffer into memory (60–3600).
NOODLR.Media.PushSegment.Name: Segment length (seconds)
NOODLR.Media.PushSegment.Hint: Length of each recorded capture segment before transcription.
NOODLR.Media.NoMic: No microphone API available in this browser.
NOODLR.Keybindings.ToggleChatPanel.Name: Toggle Noodlr chat panel
NOODLR.Keybindings.ToggleChatPanel.Hint: Open or close the Noodlr chat panel.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.Menu.Label: Diagnostics
NOODLR.Diagnostics.Title: Diagnostics & Statistics
NOODLR.Diagnostics.Intro: Concrete numbers behind the 'smart' features: whether memory writes are landing in LanceDB, and how much work retrieval/rerank/ingest are actually doing this session.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.RagDisabled: Memory is disabled. Enable it in the Memory & Knowledge window to see live silo counts and run the self-test.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.SelfTest.Hint: Writes a uniquely-tagged marker document into the 'docs' silo, then searches it back — proving embeddings + storage + query all work end-to-end.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.SelfTest.Ok: Pass: wrote {inserted} row(s) and read the marker back ({mode} search).
NOODLR.Diagnostics.SelfTest.NotFound: Wrote the marker but the query (returned {hits} hit(s)) didn't include it. Check that the same embedding model is used for ingest and query, and that the 'docs' silo isn't misconfigured.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.SelfTest.Disabled: Memory is disabled — enable it first.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.RagQuery.Hint: Run a search against memory and see the raw hits the model would receive — score, silo/source, and full text — with no AI in the loop. Great for checking what the GM is actually pulling from the rules or lore.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.RagQuery.Placeholder: Ask memory something (e.g. 'grappling rules', 'who is the baron?')
NOODLR.Diagnostics.RagQuery.NoQuery: Type something to search for first.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.EmbedderHint: Loads the bundled offline embedding model in your browser (no service, no API key). The first run downloads the model into memory and can take several seconds; later runs are instant. Use this to confirm Memory Lite works on this machine before relying on it.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.EmbedTest.Running: Loading model and embedding a probe sentence… (first run may take several seconds)
NOODLR.Diagnostics.EmbedTest.Ok: Pass: produced a {dims}-dim vector in {ms} ms. The in-browser embedder works here.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.EmbedTest.Fail: Embedder failed: {error}. If this mentions WASM, CSP, or fetch, the ORT/model assets couldn't load under Foundry's security policy.
NOODLR.Diagnostics.EmbedTest.NotLite: This test only applies to the RAG Lite backend. Switch the Memory backend to RAG Lite (Memory & Knowledge window) to run it.
NOODLR.Behavior.Enabled.Name: Behavioral automation
NOODLR.Behavior.Enabled.Hint: When a rules module decides a creature flees, surrenders, or is spared, Noodlr gives it words. The outcome itself is already settled by the rules module; this only supplies the voice.
NOODLR.Behavior.Banter.Name: Let creatures talk during a fight
NOODLR.Behavior.Banter.Hint: The occasional taunt from an automated creature, chosen to suit whoever it is aimed at. How often depends on the creature: clever and charismatic things run their mouths, wise ones keep quiet, and anything with no language never speaks. Read aloud only if voice is already switched on.
NOODLR.Behavior.PromptHint: How the AI is told to voice a creature that flees, yields, or tries to talk its way out. It is given the verb, the creature, and who it is dealing with, and asked only for the words — never for a mechanical outcome.
NOODLR.Capability.Enabled.Name: Read written abilities for the rules module
NOODLR.Capability.Enabled.Hint: Let a rules module hand Noodlr the abilities written on a creature's sheet — Regeneration, Pack Tactics, a monster's own Multiattack — so the AI can turn them into rules that module can actually run. Each distinct wording is read once and remembered, so a scene of twenty goblins costs one reading. The rules module has its own switch for this and ships it off, so both ends have to be on before anything is spent.
NOODLR.Capability.Model.Name: Model used to read abilities
NOODLR.Capability.Model.Hint: Leave blank to use the chat model above. Worth setting: reading a stat block is a different job from narrating, and a model chosen for following a strict format may be cheaper, faster, or simply better at it than the one you want telling the story.
NOODLR.Capability.Concurrency.Name: Abilities read at once
NOODLR.Capability.Concurrency.Hint: How many abilities to read in parallel when a scene loads. Higher is faster and costs exactly the same; too high and your provider starts refusing requests, which Noodlr waits out rather than failing. Four is a safe default.
NOODLR.Capability.PromptHint: How the AI is told to turn one written ability into rules. It is given the ability's text plus the real numbers off the sheet, and asked for machine-readable rules in a fixed vocabulary — never for prose, and never for a decision about what happens at the table. The vocabulary itself comes from the rules module and is added automatically, so editing this cannot break the format; it changes the instructions, not the language.
